title: The CLF-C02 exam: format, domains and scoring

kcs.statement: CLF-C02 has 65 questions in 90 minutes; 50 are scored and 15 are unscored pilot items that are not marked, so every question must be treated as if it counts.
Results are reported as a scaled score from 100 to 1,000 with 700 as the passing mark, and the scaled score is not the same as the raw percentage of questions answered correctly.

Scored content is weighted Cloud Concepts 24%, Security and Compliance 30%, Cloud Technology and Services 34% and Billing, Pricing and Support 12%, so of 50 scored items about 17 come from Domain 3 and about 6 from Domain 4.

Scoring is compensatory (you pass on the overall score, not on each domain), and an unanswered question counts as wrong with no extra penalty for a wrong guess, so every question should get an answer.

problem_ideas: Given the four domain weights, compute how many of the 50 scored questions to expect from each domain.
A learner says 'I need 70% right to pass because the pass mark is 700'; identify what is wrong with that claim.
A candidate scores 'Needs improvement' on Billing but passes overall; explain how that is possible under compensatory scoring.
With 3 minutes left and 6 unanswered questions, decide whether to leave them blank or guess, and say why.
A learner wants to skip Domain 4 entirely; estimate the maximum share of the scored exam they are giving up.
A friend recognises an odd question and assumes it is unscored, so skips it; explain why that is a bad bet.
Rank the four domains by how many scored questions each contributes and pick which to revise first with two days left.
